title: Kestrel Runner — launch spot
storyboard:
# Kestrel Runner — launch spot

Length 12 seconds at 30 fps. Deliver three cuts: 16:9 (1920x1080), 9:16 (1080x1920), 1:1 (1080x1080).

## Shot 1 (0:00–0:03) Product hero
- A teal running shoe with an orange sole slides in from the left over a dark night-city background.
- The shoe is fully inside the frame by 0:01.
- Caption reads exactly: Run the city
- The caption is fully visible by 0:01.

## Shot 2 (0:03–0:07) Detail
- Close-up of the orange sole, same teal and orange colourway as shot 1.
- The KESTREL wordmark is absent at 0:03 and fully visible by 0:05.
- A price tag reads exactly: €149 and is visible at 0:04 and at 0:06.

## Shot 3 (0:07–0:12) Call to action
- Headline reads exactly: Out 28 November
- A button labelled exactly: Get early access, fully visible by 0:09.
- The KESTREL wordmark is visible throughout shot 3.
- On the 9:16 cut, no text or button sits in the bottom 35% or the top 14% of the frame.
- On every cut, all text stays fully inside the frame.

versions.summary:
I've written `src/Video.tsx`: a 12-second spot at 30 fps (360 frames) in three shots, built from one component that lays itself out for 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1. I haven't rendered it or run Kane against it. The timings and safe zones below come from the layout numbers in the code, not from checking actual frames.

**Shot 1 — Product hero (frames 0–89)**
- A teal shoe with an orange sole, drawn in SVG, slides in from the left over a night city. The city has lit windows, blinking antenna lights and slow parallax, with speed lines behind the shoe.
- The shoe finishes moving at frame 26, so it's fully inside the frame by 0:01 on all three cuts.
- "Run the city" fades and rises into place, fully visible by frame 26.

**Shot 2 — Detail (frames 90–209)**
- A close-up of the toe and sole that slowly pushes in, with a light sweep across the sole. It uses the same drawing as shot 1, so the colours match.
- "€149" sits on a white hang tag that drops in and settles. It's fully visible from frame 106 to the end of the shot, which covers both 0:04 and 0:06.
- "KESTREL" is invisible at 0:03 and comes into focus over frames 108–138, so it's fully visible well before 0:05.

I fixed the failing 9:16 check. Kane applied the "keep text out of the bottom 35%" rule to the whole 9:16 cut, not just shot 3. In shot 2 the "KESTREL" wordmark sat at 64.5% of the frame height, so it fell in that bottom band. I haven't re-rendered it myself; Kane re-checks automatically.

The change only affects shot 2 on the 9:16 cut:
- **Wordmark:** moved to the top, from 16% to about 23% of the height. That puts it in the dark area above the shoe close-up, clear of the 14% top band.
- **Price tag:** now hangs on a short string just below the wordmark, from about 25% to 38% of the height, so the string no longer crosses the wordmark. It still drops in by about 0:03.5 and stays up to the cut, so it's visible at 0:04 and 0:06.

The timing of the wordmark and price tag is unchanged, and the 16:9 and 1:1 cuts are untouched. On the 9:16 cut, all text and the button now stay between 14% and 65% of the frame height.
